item.research_question: How can the compressive strength of the NbMoCrTiAl refractory high-entropy alloy be improved for high-temperature structural applications while maintaining oxidation resistance?
item.material_system: NbMoCrTiAl high entropy alloy matrix with in-situ formed TiC and Al2O3 reinforcement particles
item.processing_route: High energy planetary ball milling for 39 h at 300 rpm with stearic acid as process control agent, followed by spark plasma sintering (SPS) at 1700 °C under 30 MPa axial pressure for 30 min
item.test_conditions: Room temperature compression tests at a strain rate of 10^-3 s^-1 on cylindrical specimens (4 mm diameter, 6 mm height)
key_findings: The composite achieved a compressive fracture strength of 1542 MPa, an increase of approximately 50% compared to the as-cast NbMoCrTiAl HEA (1010 MPa).
The microstructure consists of 60.8 vol.% BCC solid solution, 32.2 vol.% TiC particles, and 7.0 vol.% Al2O3 particles.
The average particle sizes were measured to be approximately 4.60 μm for TiC and 1.57 μm for Al2O3.
The composite exhibited a typical cleavage fracture mode without ductility at room temperature.
Mo and Cr elements are enriched almost entirely in the BCC phase, while Ti and C are enriched in the TiC phases.
No apparent debonding was found between the dispersed particles and the HEA matrix, indicating good bonding.
item.mechanism: The remarkable increase in mechanical properties is attributed to three main factors: second phase strengthening from the brittle ceramic reinforcements, grain refinement strengthening due to the powder metallurgy process and hard phase barriers, and solid solution strengthening caused by interstitial atoms (C and O) and solute Nb in the TiC lattice.
item.limitations: The authors state that the NbMoCrTiAl RHEA is a brittle alloy without ductility, evidenced by the cleavage fracture mode and high VEC (4.96) values.
item.future_work: The authors suggest the P/M NbMoCrTiAl HEA composite could be considered a promising high temperature structural material due to its superior oxidation resistance and mechanical properties.
quotes: With the presence of approximately 7.0 vol. % Al 2 O 3 and 32.2 vol. % TiC reinforced particles, the compressive fracture strength of the composite (1542 MPa) was increased by approximately 50% compared with that of the as-cast NbMoCrTiAl HEA.
The composite created a kind of material with highly improved compressive strength, increasing from 1010 MPa to 1542 MPa.
